hints: Introduce prefix sums p[i] for the unknown array.
Each segment constraint becomes a difference between two prefix sums.
Treat these differences as weighted graph edges and check consistency.
analogy: Each constraint is a fixed height difference between two points; following different paths must give the same height.
example: Constraints sum(1,2)=3 and sum(2,2)=1 allow prefix values [0,2,3] and array [2,1].
algorithm: For every constraint (l,r,s), add directed weighted edges from l-1 to r with weight s and from r to l-1 with weight -s. Traverse each connected component, assigning an arbitrary starting prefix value 0 and setting p[v]=p[u]+weight along edges. If an already assigned vertex gets a different required value, print IMPOSSIBLE. Otherwise output x[i]=p[i]-p[i-1]. Use 64-bit integers.
correctness: Every constraint is exactly p[r]-p[l-1]=s. Traversal enforces all such equations; a conflicting assignment proves no solution exists. If no conflict occurs, the constructed differences satisfy every edge and hence every original constraint. Separate components may choose independent offsets.
complexity: For n array elements and m constraints, time and space are O(n+m).
